exact_statement: For every Boolean sign f on a finite uniform cube and physical block B, K(f)=integral J_f=(H_nat(f)-p_empty ln(1/p_empty))/2 obeys 2[K(f)-E_y K(f_y)]=M_B^+ + C_B^+ + ell_B, where q_T=sum_{U subset B}p_{U union T}=E_y p_y(T), M_T=sum_U p_{U union T}ln(q_T/p_{U union T}), C_T=E_y p_y(T)ln(p_y(T)/q_T), plus omits T=empty, and ell_B=sum_{nonempty U subset B}p_U ln(1/p_U). All three terms are nonnegative. For B={i}, C_i^+<=2 Inf_i and ell_i<=(2/e)Inf_i. The identity telescopes in every finite physical stopping tree, with retained terminal K and cumulative channel-plus-level cost <=(2+2/e)[I(f)-E I(leaf)]. If R_nat=sum_i M_i^+ and B_nat=sum_i H_nat(S_i|S_without_i), then 0<=B_nat-R_nat<=(1+2/e)I. Moreover R_nat(y product_{j=1}^m g(x^(j)))=m B_nat(g) and I=m I(g)+1, so the optimal universal constants for R_nat/I and B_nat/I are equal. A universal R_nat<=A I implies FEI in bits with constant (A+2)/ln2 via C018; no such A is proved here.

exact_statement: For any finite probability law p, atom costs a_s>=log2(1/p_s) and nonnegative Kraft lengths l_s, let m be the mass where l_s<a_s. Then H(p)<=sum_s p_s min(a_s,l_s)+m log2(1/m)<=sum_s p_s min(a_s,l_s)+h2(m). For every integer a>=8, pad the Boolean addressing function with a address and 2^a private data coordinates to N=a+2^a+2 bits and flip its all-plus input, obtaining F_a. Put c_arith(S)=2(N-1) on nonempty S and infinity on empty S, c_inf(S)=log2(e)+sum_i_in_S log2(I(F_a)/Inf_i(F_a)), and c_level(S)=-log2(r_|S|)+log2 binom(N,|S|) for any probability prior r on levels. Then E_{p_Fa} min(c_arith,c_inf,c_level)/I(F_a)>=log2(a/2)/40, while H(F_a)/I(F_a)->4. The same lower bound holds for min(c_arith,c_mix), where c_mix is the length of any fixed subprobability prior mixture of the influence and level code laws. Thus no universal O(I) expected-cost bound exists for these three references; no queue-code or FEI claim is refuted.

exact_statement: For every Boolean seed g on m>=1 uniform core coordinates, every physical vertex x0, and r>=1 dummy padding coordinates, let F_r differ from g only at (x0,all +), let d=2^(1-m-r), and let I_core=sum of the core-coordinate influences of F_r. For every physical tree that queries only padding coordinates along the unique edited branch and stops every clean branch, the total expected entropy drop Q_pad satisfies Q_pad<=4 I_queried+(1+6/ln(2)) I_core. The core reserve is allocated once across the whole tree. If every leaf satisfies U<=b I, b>=0, where U=sum_nonempty hat f(S)^2(max{|T|:hat f(T)!=0,T contains S}-|S|), then H(F_r)<=(3+2b+6/ln(2)) I(F_r); a sufficient admission is U(g)<=b I(g) and U(F_0)<=b I(F_0). For fixed finite g and r>=2, with L the number of its nonzero Fourier coefficients and p=2^(-m-r), the padding-node drop Delta_r obeys |Delta_r/(2p)-4|<=4 L p (|m+r-3|+m+3/(2ln(2))), hence the ratio tends to 4. The point-defect padding nodes satisfy 0<=Delta<=5 Inf at every dimension. Consequently dictator one-point surgery and Maj3 tensor point defects have explicit U<=I stopping trees paid at node rate 5, with full terminal entropy retained. There is no uniform padding-node rate for arbitrary varying seeds: quadratic bent seeds of even dimension m at fixed r>=2 have Delta_r/(2p)=4+2^(1-r)(m+2r-6+3/ln(2))+O(2^(-r)*2^(1-m/2-r)). These are a padding-access theorem and its scope guards, not universal admission of arbitrary Boolean core leaves.
